identificationModule.briefTitle: Study of Sitravatinib With or Without Other Anticancer Therapies Receiving Clinical Benefit From Parent Study
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Open-label Rollover Study of Sitravatinib Alone or in Combination With Other Anticancer Therapies in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic Solid Malignancies

descriptionModule.briefSummary: A Study of Sitravatinib Alone or in Combination with Other Anticancer Therapies in Advanced or Metastatic Malignancies
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Sitravatinib is a spectrum-selective receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor that inhibits several closely related RTKs including the TAM family (Tyro3/Axl/MERTK), VEGFR2, KIT, and MET.

The current study is designed to allow continued access to sitravatinib and to evaluate the safety and tolerability of sitravatinib alone or in combination with other anticancer therapies in patients who are deriving clinical benefit in a previous parent clinical trial.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Treatment Related Adverse Events.
primaryOutcomes.description: An AE is any reaction, side effect or other undesirable medical event that occurs during participation in a clinical trial, regardless of treatment group or suspected causal relationship to study treatment. Assessment of AEs will include type, incidence, severity (graded by the National Cancer Institute \[NCI\] Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events \[CTCAE, Version 5.0\]), timing, seriousness, and relatedness to study treatment. A treatment-emergent AE (TEAE) is an AE that occurs after the first dose of any study treatment or any pre-existing condition that increases in severity after the first dose of study treatment.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Currently receiving sitravatinib single- agent or in combination with other therapeutic agent(s) in another Mirati- sponsored protocol
* Currently tolerating the treatment regimen in the parent protocol
* Experiencing clinical benefit with or without prior radiographic progression from the treatment regimen in the parent protocol in the opinion of the investigator and the investigator determines that continuing treatment is in the patient's best interest

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known or suspected presence of other cancer
* Other life- threatening illness or organ system dysfunction compromising safety evaluation
